newsitem.title: USA: Household product stocks weigh stock split option.
newsitem.headline: Household product stocks weigh stock split option.

text.p: The stocks of several major players in the household product sector have been climbing into the $100 range, hitting 52-week highs and raising the question: When are they going to split?
Dow industrials component Procter & Gamble Co was rising steadily last week with the rest of the market, ending Friday at 107-1/8. In midday trading on Monday, the stock was off 7/8 to 106-1/4.
The company said it had not made a decision yet on a possible split.
"We would begin considering it once we see that the stock is over 100 and it is going to stay there," said Linda Ulrey, a P&G spokeswoman.
Clorox scaled the 100 peak, with shares already at 108, up 1/8 on Monday. But Clorox does not have any plans yet to split the stock, a spokesperson said.
"It is something that we look at from time to time but do not have any current plans," he said.
Colgate-Palmolive Co also has been on a steady uphill climb, trading on Monday up 3/4 at 95-1/2, just a point shy of its 52-week high.
A Colgate spokesperson said the company had no comment on any potential split.
Analysts said a stock split, while it may be a statement of confidence on the part of the company, matters most to smaller investors who might not make an investment based on the loftier valuations.
William Steele, an analyst at Dean Witter, said most mutual funds and institutional investors "really don't care...it doesn't change the earnings."
But Steele said he considers the 100-mark critical and expects some of the companies in question to split soon.
"Given where the market is in general I would say the 100 range is where they are looking," he said.
